english_retrieval.title: Servant leadership can help to restore trust in public institutions
english_retrieval.snippet: # Servant leadership can help to restore trust in public institutions. A collapsed bridge in Minneapolis and a conversation about leadership. As our nation prepares to elect new leaders, there is an important lesson worth remembering: leadership is not primarily about authority, power or winning. Rather than asking, “How can others help me succeed?” servant leaders ask, “How can I help others succeed?” They measure success not by personal recognition or power, but by whether the people and institutions they lead become stronger, more capable and more trusted. ### *Related: Middle Aisle: A test of leadership at the Minnesota Legislature*. As commissioner of the Minnesota Department of Transportation after the collapse, I witnessed firsthand the grief, anger and uncertainty that followed. Success required a team of servant leaders — people who placed the needs of citizens above personal recognition or political advantage. Decisions were made not for personal or political gain, but for the benefit of the people we served.
